status.evidence: According to Companies House records, Microlise Group PLC is currently an active public limited company registered under company number 11553192 [.

claims.claim: Tesco integrated a comprehensive suite of Microlise software across its transport operations—including its Reading distribution centre, which dispatches up to 500 vehicles daily—to implement real-time tracking that monitors the exact location and live status of each vehicle at any given time.

Microlise delivers its OEM telematics and real-time tracking platform globally through long-term manufacturer partnerships, including a collaboration with Tata Motors (Tata Fleetman) since 2014 for the Indian market, and a white-labeled fleet management telematics suite for MAN Truck & Bus UK.

In a fleet performance project documented by Microlise, Carlsberg UK utilized the Microlise Fleet Performance platform to monitor driving styles via KPIs such as harsh acceleration and time-in-green-band, which achieved a 4.8% fuel saving in the first year and an additional 1% in the second year.

In another application, Roberts Bakery deployed the Microlise Driver Performance Management (DPM) app alongside Journey Management for its fleet of over 160 drivers, utilizing a smartphone app for driver self-monitoring and real-time planned-versus-actual route comparisons to feed back into its Paragon Routing and Scheduling software.
claims.note: The integration and feedback loop with Paragon Routing and Scheduling software is unverified.

claims.claim: The company achieved Transport Certification Australia (TCA) type-approval for its telematics hardware, following an independent assessment demonstrating compliance with strict functional and technical specifications.

Microlise Group PLC deployed its critical in-cab hardware infrastructure, Driver Behaviour Information module, and integrated solutions as part of a renewed long-term commercial fleet management contract with Maritime Transport.

The company reports that it maintains third-party verified ISO 9001, ISO 20000, and ISO 27001 certifications alongside a Cyber Essentials badge, encrypting client telematics and personally identifiable information (PII) using AES256 at rest and HTTPS/SFTP in transit within UK data centres.
claims.note: The details regarding the encryption of client telematics and PII data using AES256 at rest and HTTPS/SFTP in transit within UK data centres could not be confirmed in the published sources.
claims.source: Microlise FAQs and Certification Benefits pages

claims.claim: An independent incident case study documented that following a ransomware attack via unauthorized VPN access on 31 October 2024, Microlise Group PLC completed a 12-week incident response engagement with NCC Group to eradicate the threat actor, deploy EDR monitoring, and rebuild its Active Directory.
claims.source: NCC Group Case Study: Ransomware Incident Response for Leading Transport Tech Provider Microlise

claims.claim: A large-scale deployment at Tesco's distribution network utilized Microlise's real-time tracking and Driver Performance App to manage high-volume logistics (Microlise Tesco Case Study).

The company reports that 58% of UK large heavy goods vehicle (HGV) fleet operators (defined as fleets with more than 500 vehicles) use the Microlise platform, and its enterprise client base includes organisations representing 88% of the UK grocery retail market by market share.
claims.source: Microlise Admission to Trading on AIM / London Stock Exchange Announcement

claims.claim: Microlise signed new and expanded contracts with UK fleet operators Goldstar Heathrow (a new 5-year agreement covering its entire fleet of 170 vehicles), One Stop, and Romac, representing a combined contract value of over £2 million.
claims.source: Motor Transport (https://motortransport.co.uk) and FCA RNS announcement

claims.claim: The company reports a 58% UK market share among large (500+) heavy goods vehicle (HGV) fleets, including 88% of UK grocery retailers, alongside an adjusted group revenue increase from £81.0m to £84.0m (a 3.7% YoY increase) for the 12 months ended 31 December 2025 as disclosed in its Investors Report (https://www.microlise.com/investors/).
claims.corrected: The company reports a 58% UK market share among large (500+) heavy goods vehicle (HGV) fleets, including 88% of UK grocery retailers, alongside an adjusted group revenue increase to £84.0m (a 3.7% YoY increase) for the 12 months ended 31 December 2025 as disclosed in its Investors Report (https://www.microlise.com/investors/).
claims.source: Microlise Investors Page (https://www.microlise.com/investors/) and London Stock Exchange filings. The historical 58% market share and 88% grocery retail stats date back to their 2021 IPO Admission document rather than originating fresh within the FY25 metrics context, but more crucially, the baseline group revenue increased *to* £84.0m (from £81.0m is not explicitly in the summary data, though the 3.7% YoY growth matches).

claims.claim: The company reports in a London Stock Exchange Statement (https://www.londonstockexchange.com/news-article/SAAS/results-for-the-year-ended-31-december-2025/17591207) that for the full year ended 31 December 2025, its adjusted EBITDA was £8.3m, reflecting revenue headwinds from lower OEM volumes, while ending the period with cash and cash equivalents of £16.7m.
claims.source: London Stock Exchange Regulatory News Service (RNS) Statement (https://www.londonstockexchange.com/news-article/SAAS/results-for-the-year-ended-31-december-2025/17591207)

claims.claim: A long-term original equipment manufacturer (OEM) partnership established in 2008 with MAN Truck & Bus UK to provide a white-labeled MAN Fleet Management telematics solution, as reported by Microlise.

A long-term leasing partnership with Ryder, which reached a milestone of 5,000 vehicle connections using pre-installed Microlise telematics systems on rental and lease fleets, as reported by Microlise in May 2019.
claims.note: The exact publication date of 'May 2019' for the 5,000 milestone announcement remains unconfirmed in public release metadata, although the partnership itself and the milestone numbers are valid.

status.evidence: According to records from Companies House and Company Check, Trackunit Telematics Ltd (Company No. 05127441) is officially dissolved, while its parent global brand Trackunit was acquired by majority owner Goldman Sachs Alternatives in 2025.

claims.claim: Trackunit publishes a Service Level Agreement offering a Premium SLA tier that guarantees a 99.8% uptime and API availability threshold for its core telematics services.

The company announced the launch of its 5G-ready Spot IoT device designed to provide cellular tracking and GPS location data for non-powered fleet machinery with a configurable messaging transmission capacity.

An independent industry review published by Tommaso Maria Ricci in September 2026 documented that a regional civil contractor with a $40 million heavy equipment fleet deployed equipment telematics and predictive maintenance through configured vendor software, including Trackunit, achieving a 35% drop in unplanned downtime, a 14% reduction in total maintenance costs, and an 8% decline in fuel consumption through optimized operating patterns.
claims.corrected: An independent industry review published by Tommaso Maria Ricci in September 2026 documented that a regional civil contractor with a $40 million heavy equipment fleet deployed equipment telematics and predictive maintenance through configured vendor software, including Trackunit, achieving a 25 to 50 percent drop in unplanned downtime, a 10 to 20 percent reduction in total maintenance costs, and an 8% decline in fuel consumption through optimized operating patterns.
claims.note: The original review by Ricci actually lists outcomes as a 25 to 50 percent drop in unplanned downtime and a 10 to 20 percent reduction in total maintenance costs. The 8% figure for fuel consumption was also not specifically specified under his documented outcomes for predictive maintenance.

claims.claim: The company reports that its core platform, Trackunit Manager, built on its IrisX Construction Operating Data Platform, standardizes multi-source mixed-fleet metrics—such as machine health, utilization, runtime, fuel consumption, and jobsite activity—allowing operators to draw custom geo-fences that feed real-time location-based analytics to reduce idle time by 20% to 30%.

The company reports that its Trackunit Raw (TU600) hardware configuration features an embedded global roaming eSIM, a CAN bus interface supporting CAN J1939 and CAN Open protocols, built-in GPS, an internal backup battery lasting 2-3 weeks, and Bluetooth 5.0 connectivity to establish local sensor networks.
claims.corrected: The company reports that its Trackunit Raw (TU600) hardware configuration features an embedded global roaming eSIM, a CAN bus interface supporting CAN J1939 and CAN Open protocols, built-in GPS, an internal backup battery, and Bluetooth 5.0 connectivity to establish local sensor networks.
claims.note: The 2-3 weeks battery life specification is unverified for the TU600 configuration (the TU600 installation guide specifies a 720 mAh backup battery without confirming a 2-3 week runtime limit, whereas CAN protocols J1939 / CAN Open are documented under the newer TU700 series specs).

claims.claim: In a fleet migration project, French rental company Accès Industrie deployed Trackunit hardware configurations across a fleet of over 6,000 machines, utilizing Trackunit's documented, streamlined setup to transition rapidly after their previous telematics provider shut down.
Trackunit reports that its core operating engine, the IRIS Platform, is officially certified against the ISO/IEC 27001:2022 standard for information security management systems.
claims.corrected: Trackunit reports that its core operating engine, the IrisX Platform, is officially certified against the ISO/IEC 27001:2022 standard for information security management systems.

claims.claim: Trackunit provides pre-formulated Data Processing Agreements (DPA) and Standard Contractual Clauses (SCC) designed to ensure that data flows conform directly to European Data Protection Board (EDPB) and General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) requirements.

The company reports successful implementation of its API integration to connect and flow telematics data directly into Hugg & Hall Equipment Company's internal Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system.
claims.note: flow telematics data directly into Hugg & Hall Equipment Company's internal Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system via API integration

claims.claim: Trackunit partnered with Sunbelt Rentals UK & Ireland to expand telematics connectivity to over 20,000 mixed assets on its Trackunit IrisX platform as part of their five-year growth strategy.
Trackunit acquired Satrak UK Ltd in 2018 to establish its presence as a primary machine telematics enterprise in the UK market, incorporating Satrak's Leeds operations and adding to its global base.

In June 2018, Trackunit's UK subsidiary, Trackunit Ltd, acquired the machine telematics provider Satrak UK Ltd to consolidate its position in the region, as outlined in the Trackunit A/S Annual Report.

The group's parent annual report filed by Galaxy Holdco ApS in May 2023 detailed corporate reorganization steps taken to consolidate its UK business operations under Trackunit Ltd and strike off Trackunit Telematics Ltd.

Sunbelt Rentals UK & Ireland and Trackunit extended their strategic partnership in November 2025 to surpass 20,000 connected assets deployed under the Sunbelt 4.0 strategy, using the Trackunit IrisX platform via an AI-driven customer portal and Fleet API.

Trackunit entered into a strategic technical partnership with Bosch Rexroth in April 2025 to integrate the Rexroth BODAS Connect OTA Update Platform with Trackunit Manager on the IrisX ecosystem to provide secure, remote machine updates for OEM customers.
The company reports a physical UK office footprint located at 27 Greville Street, London.
claims.source: Trackunit Contact Official Page & UK Companies House Filings

claims.claim: Trackunit’s official documentation states that technical support for its UK customers is limited to standard operational business hours (Monday–Thursday from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM and Friday from 8:00 AM to 3:30 PM), rather than 24/7 coverage.
